annotation.title_clean: Robots on Sale: The effect of tax policy on robot adoption and employment
annotation.title_en: Robots on Sale: The effect of tax policy on robot adoption and employment
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Adachi, D.; Kawaguchi, D.; Saito, Y.U.
annotation.summary_en: RIETI discussion paper using Japan's Tax Credit for Promoting Productivity-Enhancing Equipment Investment and a new firm-level survey of industrial robot ownership to estimate causal effects of robot adoption. Tax-eligible firms adopted more robots, and adoption did not reduce employment, instead raising it after 1-3 years.
key_provisions_or_claims: Tax-credit-eligible firms significantly increased industrial robot investment.
Robot adoption did not reduce total or production worker employment.
Employment and sales rose 1-3 years after adoption.
Firms reallocate workers to non-robot tasks when adopting robots.
Careful organizational design allows efficiency gains without labor market disruption.
